name: Quantum-dot brain voltage probe
subtitle: glowing dots that report every neuron's firing

effects.effect: crystals a few nanometres wide glow in a colour set purely by their size
an electric field splits a glowing gas's colour lines

effect: crystals a few nanometres wide glow in a colour set purely by their size
how: Electrodes in the brain hear only a few hundred neurons each, while a mind-reading interface would want many thousands. Crystal dots a few nanometres wide, slipped into the membranes of nerve cells, change their glow when the cell fires, because an electric field shifts the colour such tiny crystals give off; a fibre-optic camera then reads thousands of neurons at once by their flicker.
obstacle: Getting the dots to sit stably in cell membranes without harming neurons, and doing it in a living human brain.
why: Membrane dots reported voltage in cultured cells; never used to read a living brain.
real: Colloidal quantum dots in neuronal membranes detected depolarization optically in cultured cells (Nano Letters 2019), but no in vivo brain-interface use has been shown.
